merger_name: Brookfield Corporation Ltd – Brookfield Corporation and Brookfield Wealth Solutions Ltd

anzsic_codes.name: Other Auxiliary Finance and Investment Services

merger_description:
Brookfield Corporation (**Brookfield**) is a Canadian incorporated global investment firm focused on building long-term wealth for institutions and individuals around the world. Brookfield has three core businesses: Alternative Asset Management, Wealth Solutions, and its Operating Businesses. Brookfield is a public company, co-listed on the New York Stock Exchange (**NYSE**) and the Toronto Stock Exchange (**TSX**). Brookfield, via its various subsidiaries and managed funds, has business activities and interests in Australia and invests across a range of sectors, including infrastructure, energy, real estate and private equity.

Brookfield Wealth Solutions (**BWS**) is an investment-led insurance organisation, focused on securing the financial futures of individuals and institutions through a range of retirement services, wealth protection products, and tailored capital solutions. Through its operating subsidiaries, BWS offers a broad range of insurance products and services, including life insurance and annuities, and personal and commercial property and casualty insurance. BWS is incorporated under the laws of Bermuda. BWS is also a public company, co-listed on the NYSE and the TSX with a market capitalisation of approximately US $14.95 billion (as of 21 August 2026).

Brookfield Corporation Ltd (**New Brookfield**) is a new company incorporated by BWS under the laws of Bermuda. It currently holds no assets and has no business activities.

The parties have entered into a Transaction Agreement pursuant to which Brookfield and BWS will be combined under the common ownership of a new parent company, New Brookfield

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application, and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition. There will be no horizontal consolidation, removal of a
competitor, or change to either of Brookfield’s or BWS’ competitive
position as a result of the Acquisition.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC also considered the potential application of section
51ABD of the Act. However, the applicant submitted that one or
more of the steps that will occur to put the Acquisition into effect
may involve an acquisition that is required to be notified, and having
regard to the particular circumstances, including the consequences
of non-notification in reliance on section 51ABD if it was found not to
apply, the ACCC considers it appropriate to make a determination on
the basis that the acquisition provisions in the Act apply to the
Acquisition.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
